newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen moving sideways.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen moving sideways.

text.p: Most Polish shares rose, but losses of some heavyweights pulled the main index down and analysts saw the bourse remaining relatively flat on Friday, following post-fixing mixed continuous trade.

Some analysts said some blue-chips, which were the engine of the recent two-month growth on the Warsaw exchange, seemed fairly priced, but said the overall market, which fell 4.7 percent after the surge, was becoming attractive.
"Stocks trade at 16 times historic earnings, but if we consider future profits, P/E of many stocks is much lower," said Aleksander Jawien, a trader of Polish Development Bank.
Analysts were not sure whether the market has ended its profit-taking correction after it gained 30 percent since the beginning of the year or whether it would see more falls next week.
The main market's WIG index eased 25 points, or 0.1 percent, to 17,514.9, and turnover rose 5.8 percent to 201.6 million zlotys on all three markets as 58 issues rose, 17 fell and 15 were flat.
Some analysts said a recent dollar rise against the zloty was making Warsaw bourse look more attractive for foreign investors.
But others said the 30 percent surge had to trigger fall deeper than those experienced so far and expected the profit-taking to pull the WIG index to 16,500 in the next two weeks.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 30.5-million-zlotys with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,785.7 points, 1.6 percent above the regular session close.
NFI units were flat in a 27.2-million-zloty regular trade but fell 0.9 percent in a 15-million-zloty continuous trade turnover.
